before: Keep the phishing variants clear on the exam: Phishing = Email; Vishing = Voice / Phone; Smishing = SMS / Text message; Spear phishing = Targeted individual; Whaling = Senior executive.

before: Spear Phishing is an email-based social engineering attack tailored to a specific individual, team, or organization using gathered intelligence to craft believable, context-specific lures, unlike generic bulk phishing.
after: Spear phishing tailors deceptive communications to a particular individual, team or organization. The researched, personalized email in this scenario fits that targeted form of phishing; not all phishing is generic bulk mail.
justification: Targeted phishing is not exclusively email. Preserve the actual tailored-email case without inventing an evil-twin mechanism or changing the example transaction.

justification: Targeted phishing is not exclusively email. Preserve the actual tailored-email case without inventing an evil-twin mechanism or changing the example transaction.

before: Automated voice response attacks represent vishing rather than email-based spear phishing.
after: Voice attacks can also be targeted. This offered description specifies automated voice interaction, whereas the stated attack uses a personalized email.
justification: Targeted phishing is not exclusively email. Preserve the actual tailored-email case without inventing an evil-twin mechanism or changing the example transaction.

before: การใช้เสียงหลอกลวงทางโทรศัพท์คือ Vishing ไม่ใช่ Spear Phishing

before: Credential Stuffing เป็นการนำรหัสผ่านที่รั่วไหลไปสุ่มล็อกอินเข้าระบบทางออนไลน์

justification: Credential stuffing replays stolen credential pairs rather than random password guessing.

before: An employee uses a password manager to generate distinct 20-character random passwords for their personal social media and corporate email, ensuring a breach of one never compromises the other.
after: An employee uses an approved manager to generate distinct random 20-character passwords for personal social media and corporate email. A stolen password from one service then does not supply the other service’s password; other takeover paths still require controls.
justification: Unique passwords limit same-pair replay, not every cross-system compromise; retain only verified source attribution.

before: พนักงานใช้ Password Manager สร้างรหัสผ่านสุ่ม 20 ตัวอักษรที่ไม่ซ้ำกันระหว่างบัญชีโซเชียลมีเดียส่วนตัวกับอีเมลบริษัท ทำให้หากบริการภายนอกถูกแฮก ข้อมูลบริษัทก็จะไม่ได้รับผลกระทบ

justification: Unique passwords limit same-pair replay, not every cross-system compromise; retain only verified source attribution.

before: Avoiding password reuse and using password managers prevents credential stuffing attacks from external breaches.
after: Distinct passwords limit replay of a breached password across services; an approved password manager can support this practice.
justification: Unique passwords limit same-pair replay, not every cross-system compromise; retain only verified source attribution.

before: NIST SP 800-63B and ISC2 recommend: Long passphrases, no arbitrary periodic resets unless compromise is suspected, and strictly avoiding password reuse across systems.
after: NIST password guidance distinguishes arbitrary periodic changes from changes required on compromise and supports distinct passwords across services. A password manager can help manage those secrets.
justification: Unique passwords limit same-pair replay, not every cross-system compromise; retain only verified source attribution.

before: แนวทางของ NIST SP 800-63B และ ISC2: ใช้ Passphrase ขนาดยาว, ไม่บังคับเปลี่ยนรหัสผ่านเป็นประจำหากไม่มีเหตุสงสัยว่าถูกแฮก, และห้ามใช้รหัสผ่านซ้ำกันโดยเด็ดขาด

justification: Unique passwords limit same-pair replay, not every cross-system compromise; retain only verified source attribution.

before: A Key Risk Indicator (KRI) is a forward-looking, leading metric that provides an early warning signal of elevated risk exposure, allowing organizations to take preemptive corrective action before an incident occurs.
after: KRIs communicate risk exposure and can be leading, current or lagging depending on use. This question specifically asks for forward-looking warning: increasing overdue critical flaws on exposed systems is the offered condition relevant to possible exploitation, not proof that compromise is imminent.
justification: KRIs can be leading, current or lagging. This stem specifically asks for forward-looking exposure; historical data is not universally nonpredictive.

justification: KRIs can be leading, current or lagging. This stem specifically asks for forward-looking exposure; historical data is not universally nonpredictive.

justification: KRIs can be leading, current or lagging. This stem specifically asks for forward-looking exposure; historical data is not universally nonpredictive.

after:

A single result alone does not prove improvement, a durable culture or that training caused a change; comparable repeated observations and context are needed.
Option B is incorrect. Slide completion numbers measure administrative compliance attendance, not operational vigilance.
Option C is incorrect. Spam-block counts describe a technical filtering result rather than directly observing employee reporting behavior. The filtering service need not be a physical hardware appliance.
